title: First Eckstine rehearsal in New York: the saxophones and trumpets
summary: He and Tommy Potter reach the June 1944 rehearsal of the seventeen-piece band with Parker, Lucky Thompson, Leo Parker, Buddy Anderson and Dizzy Gillespie.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: But back to where we were, about the telegram that I got from Billy Eckstine to come to New York and join this band. Immediately, I began to pack my suitcase, and called Tommy Potter, and we got together and went to New York. We had a rehearsal in Ringold(?) Studios, I think it was on a Wednesday. I'll have to look at the telegram;; I think it was in June, about June 6th or something, of 1944. And the rehearsal was called something like 1 o'clock.

So we get into New York, and we go up to this rehearsal, and here are all... There were a lot of musicians there. I found out that we were to have a 17-piece band. So I'm being introduced to the different people in the band. The reed section was Charlie Parker on alto saxophone. They had a young fellow that was from Kansas City, and everybody called him Junior, but I can't remember what his real name was. [JOHN JACKSON] There was Charlie Parker and Junior on alto saxophones.
They had a fellow named Tommy Crump, a very good tenor saxophone player who had been with Earl Hines' band. He was

on second tenor. On first tenor we had Lucky Thompson. On baritone, we had a young fellow who before had been playing alto saxophone, but he wanted to get in the band when the band was being organized, so Billy Eckstine asked him if he would play baritone saxophone, and he agreed to do it, and Billy bought him a baritone, and so he became the baritone saxophone player. [LEO PARKER] So those were the five saxophones.

In the trumpet section, we had on first trumpet Gail Brockman. On second trumpet, Buddy Anderson, a fine, fine trumpet player. Buddy Anderson was from Oklahoma City, but he had come from Jay McShann's band, as well as Charlie Parker. Buddy Anderson played second trumpet. Shorty McConnell, formerly with the Earl Hines band, played third trumpet. And fourth trumpet was Dizzy Gillespie.
